The enterprise

JARVIS arbitrages the gap between the micro-cost of AI compute and the market value of B2B digital deliverables: instead of selling human hours, it manufactures two product lines at scale — hyper-personalized B2B lead enrichment (scraped, validated decision-maker data plus LLM-written outreach tailored to each prospect) and programmatic SEO (autonomously built, long-tail landing pages fed by live data streams) — produced by a self-orchestrating workforce of 110 specialist AI agents organized in a seven-universe modular hierarchy under a central automaton that perceives, proposes and replicates only within hard budgets. Launched with zero capital on open-source automation and an automated outbound sales engine that converts retainer clients, the company reinvests a fixed share of every month's net profit through a compliance-gated Investment Automaton (Pillar 3a + IBKR ETF dollar-cost averaging under Swiss private-investor guardrails), marching from bootstrap to sovereignty — cloud tools first, owned local hardware last — while every external, financial or high-stakes action, including each act of machine self-replication, passes through The Nexus: a human-in-the-loop gate where the founder's keystroke is the only key that turns automation into action.

◈ Bounded autonomy
